# Port CI kit manifest: the files a fork's CI needs (tools/port-ci-kit.py). One path per line, relative
# to the repository root. Generated by `port-ci-kit.py trace` from a real green ci-gates run, then reviewed.
# Not a release of the migrator -- only what tools/ci-gates.py opens or passes on a command line.
# Added by hand (not traced; a green run on a version branch's CI is the check): ci-gates --shipped's shipped-gate.py,
# layer-deps.py (sibling_jars: a version branch's --shipped boots the sibling ports' jars), fork-kind.py (the layer
# refusal every fork-taking tool runs) and checkout-lock.py (ci-gates --mc's one-run-per-checkout lock), and the harness
# rename table of each version (port_gates.harness_table reads templates/upstream-harness/versions/<mc>.renames.tsv).
# Also by hand: the promote job's install-manifest refresh, port-manifest.py (standard library only, self-contained),
# and the publish job's known-issues check, known-issues.py (port-publish.py's per-platform blocks-publish; standard library only).
# Also by hand: ci-gates.py's report-only audits, audit-wiring.py and audit-descriptors.py (standard library; the
# latter loads audit-mixin-targets.py beside it), audit-mixin-targets.py itself and audit-event-listeners.py with
# qtc-init.gradle (Gradle's own compile classpath, which that audit asks the JDK's javap about).
